SMTO-EXE-0135 — SMTO downloaded a file but couldn't save it

GUID: 140fa5e2-8e5e-5b6d-9716-2759ec2b609f
Slug: browser-artifact-failure
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • The web browser finished downloading the file, but SMTO couldn't save it into this task's files on the Gateway computer. The browser still has the finished download.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running the Gateway has free disk space. Saving the downloaded file fails when that computer's disk is full.
  2. Ask SMTO to save the file it already downloaded, and tell it not to click the download link again. The browser keeps the finished download until its session closes, so no second download is needed.
  3. Don't ask SMTO to close that browser session until the file is saved. Closing the browser session throws away the downloaded file it is still holding.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports that the file is saved and gives you the file.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway; the folder SMTO saves task files into on that computer may not be writable. Don't ask SMTO to download the file again from the website in the meantime.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • PlaywrightBackend._export_download hit an OS error while writing an already completed browser download into the run's artifact folder on the Gateway.

What this means

  • Download export encountered an OS error while writing to the owning artifact workspace after the browser had already retained the download. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Download export encountered an OS error while writing to the owning artifact workspace after the browser had already retained the download.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained download ID, run scope and artifact storage failure before triggering another download.

How to fix it

  • Check free disk space and permissions of the run's artifact directory under the Gateway artifact root (OF_RUN_ARTIFACT_DIR for this conversation and run) and look in the Gateway log for the OS error. Then export the same download again with browser.downloads using its download_id and as_artifact=true; do not trigger the download on the page again, and keep the session open, because stopping it releases the temporary download.
  • Check the selected Gateway artifact workspace and run scope. Retry exporting the observed download rather than triggering it again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Check the selected Gateway artifact workspace and run scope. Retry exporting the observed download rather than triggering it again.

How to verify the fix

  • The existing download is exported successfully to its owning run without repeating the external download action.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
